steps.tx: **The coenzyme map** compresses this whole module into one pattern: vitamin, active coenzyme, flagship enzymes, deficiency flag. Thiamine gives TPP for four enzymes, riboflavin gives FMN and FAD, niacin gives NAD and NADP, pantothenate gives CoA, B6 gives PLP, biotin serves carboxylases, folate gives THF carriers and B12 runs two reactions. Vitamin C stands apart as a reducing cosubstrate.
steps.say: Learn this map once and every vitamin question becomes a lookup. Vitamin to coenzyme to flagship enzyme to deficiency flag is the whole game.

steps.tx: **Stores timing** predicts the order of failure in starvation and alcohol use disorder. Thiamine empties in about two to three weeks, folate in a few months and B12 only after years, because intakes, stores and recycling differ. A patient refed after two weeks risks Wernicke long before any megaloblastic blood appears, which is why emergency protocols sequence vitamins in that order.
steps.say: Thiamine fails in weeks, folate in months, B12 in years. That order dictates emergency practice: thiamine first whenever nutrition restarts.

steps.tx: **Excess rules** for water soluble vitamins have two named exceptions. Most surplus is excreted in urine, so toxicity is uncommon, but pyridoxine megadoses cause sensory neuropathy and nicotinic acid causes prostaglandin flushing with liver injury at drug doses. Those two exceptions are exactly what examiners probe when a stem describes a supplement enthusiast with new symptoms.
steps.say: Water soluble excess usually washes out harmlessly. Two exceptions earn their place in every exam: B6 neuropathy and nicotinic acid flushing with liver injury.

steps.tx: **Hidden vitamin stems** reward pattern reading. Alcohol use disorder hides thiamine and folate, isoniazid hides B6, a strict vegan diet hides B12, raw egg white habits hide biotin, maize based poverty hides niacin, and dialysis or parenteral nutrition hides several at once. Translating the social detail into the vitamin is the tested skill, not recall alone.
steps.say: Exam stems hide vitamins inside social details. Alcohol, isoniazid, vegan diets, raw egg, maize and dialysis each point at a specific missing vitamin.

steps.tx: **Mixed deficiency** is the real world default. Poor diets, alcohol and malabsorption remove several B vitamins together, so glossitis, cheilosis, neuropathy, anaemia and confusion overlap and blur single vitamin pictures. Treatment therefore replaces broadly while targeted tests identify the dominant lack, rather than waiting for a textbook pure syndrome that rarely walks into clinic.
steps.say: Pure single deficiencies are textbook rarities; mixed deficiency is clinic reality. Replace broadly, test for the dominant lack, and do not wait for a perfect picture.

steps.tx: **Separation questions** close every set in this module. Folate versus B12 turns on neurology and methylmalonate, thiamine emergencies turn on treatment before glucose, and B6 turns on the lack and excess both injuring nerves. If you can run those three separations plus the coenzyme map from memory, the water soluble vitamins are finished.
steps.say: Finish with three separations: folate against B12, thiamine before glucose, and B6 lack against B6 excess. Master those and this module is yours.
